cards.name: Camera-relative run direction
cards.summary: Stick deflection or a tapped direction sets a camera-relative target heading and a deflection-scaled target speed
cards.behavior: Each update the target heading comes from the left stick offset around its 0x7F centre, is rotated into world space by the camera yaw and wrapped to the 12-bit circle. Target speed is the caller's movement speed scaled by the sum of the two axis offsets shifted right seven and clamped to that speed, so a gentle push walks and a full push reaches the top speed. With the stick centred, a freshly released direction button supplies the speed and a table heading, and with nothing pressed the target speed, the turn momentum and the pending heading all fall back to the current body heading.

constants.unit: stick axis units, centre of the 0 to 255 range, per update, rate unverified

cards.name: Turn momentum and soft turning
cards.summary: Small stick deflections blend the pending heading while turn rate ramps through a six-step momentum ladder
cards.behavior: A stick deflection below 96 units of magnitude blends the pending heading toward the current one by the deflection times the angular difference shifted right nine, and a pending difference above 256 also raises the walking state so the body reorients on the spot. Otherwise the momentum steps one unit per update toward the turn side, is clamped to plus or minus six, and never rests at zero once a turn has begun. Momentum plus six indexes a thirteen-entry turn-rate row; while the angular difference stays inside a window one full turn wide the body is rotated by that row value, and outside the window the heading snaps to the target and the momentum resets.

cards.name: Wall, floor and airborne probes
cards.summary: Wall contacts, ground contacts, slope tier, ledge detection and airborne touchdown all come from short rotated rays around the body
cards.behavior: The wall probe starts 356 units below the body origin and ends 452 units forward and 420 units down, both rotated into world space, and the hit normal is reduced to an 8-bit angle: contacts at or above 23 store the normal and raise the against-wall flag. The floor probe traces from 260 units below the origin to 452 units below, converts the normal to a slope angle, clamps negative angles to 1024, treats anything below 33 as ground and sets the slope flag from 23 upward. A second trace 260 units forward detects the ledge flag when it misses. An airborne probe spans 128 units above and below a point 356 units below the origin, traces downward, and on a hit with an upward normal adds the offset between that centre and the hit position to the body position, zeroes every axis smaller than 8 units so the body does not vibrate on contact, and clears the air timer. An axis-aligned fallback repeats the floor test whenever the body is airborne and not resting on the ground.

cards.name: Damage, knockback and invulnerability
cards.summary: Accepted hit flags cost one health, pick a reaction state and then grant ninety updates of immunity
cards.behavior: Incoming flags are first reduced by the invulnerability mask 0xFFFFFE0E while the timer runs, losing charge immunity as well when the body is rising, and then intersected with the flags the body currently accepts. A normal hit (mask 0x5F1) costs one health and chooses a reaction: a bounce, an electric hurt, a specialised hurt, an interrupted charge, or the default hurt; a lethal result routes to the death state. Every accepted hit raises the timer to 90 updates. Knockback copies the stored direction into acceleration at a fixed magnitude of 0x800, and the super bit drives the supercharge latch except in the immune state 44.

cards.name: Flame heat build-up
cards.summary: Flamed targets gain heat 24 per update to a cap of 96 and cool by two once the flame bit clears
cards.behavior: While a target carries the flame damage bit its heat value rises 24 per update and stops at 96. With the bit clear the value falls by 2 per update above 32 and by 1 from 32 down to zero, so a target keeps glowing briefly after the flame stops. The external variant adds 16 per update up to 80 while the bit is held, sheds 2 from 33 upward, and folds the remaining heat into a colour ramp so the longer a target burns the hotter it reads.

cards.name: Gem collection
cards.summary: Gems are worth 1, 2, 5, 10 or 25 and are written into a per-level bitset for persistence
cards.behavior: Collecting a gem records its class in a 32-slot recent ring, marks the key when the item is the key, refreshes the rotation matrix and emits a pickup particle. The class then maps to a value of 1, 2, 5, 10 or 25 which is added to both the level and the total counters and written into the per-level kill bitset, indexed by the static entity index or by the parent index for spawned ones. A gem collected at a height of 0x300 or more spawns the flying pickup entities instead of scoring in place, and the pickup sound plays at the end of the routine.

cards.name: Collectible drop arc
cards.summary: Dropped pickups pop out of a defeated enemy on a short ballistic arc and settle on the floor
cards.behavior: A drop starts 256 units above its parent with an upward velocity of 140, or 300 with a small random horizontal scatter, and a solver walks the velocity down by 10 per update while counting how many updates the pickup needs to reach the floor height. The landing point is probed from 1024 above the parent down 2048; if the probe misses, the surface angle is 24 or more, or a 200-unit radius shape test hits, the pickup drops straight from the parent instead. The remaining horizontal displacement is divided by the counted updates, so the pickup can be simulated cheaply as a stored start offset plus a per-update velocity.

cards.name: Health drops and revival
cards.summary: A hurt player can get a reviving companion from a defeated enemy instead of a plain reward orb
cards.behavior: When a defeated enemy has no scripted drop, a roll across the hundred range decides what falls out: results at or below 1 give an extra life, and results at or below 11 give the reviving companion while the player is below 3 health; everything else gives a life orb. Picking the companion up when none is already active and health is not below zero spawns it, plays its sound, sets health to exactly 1 and stores the companion pointer. Otherwise the small flying pickup is spawned instead, so the player is never given a companion that would be redundant.

cards.name: Spawn and release budgets
cards.summary: Spawned entities get a class, a clamped parent index and per-class render and update budgets; member groups free together
cards.behavior: Spawning allocates an entity slot, records its class, and derives the parent index from the parent pointer, collapsing anything above 0xFF to zero. Per-class setup then fills the property block, position, rotation, collision data and renderer bits. Small collectables get tight budgets while larger props take the whole 255 range. Releasing one entity deactivates it, and releasing a member group walks the group list and frees every live member, which is how a group of linked enemies disappears in one step.

cards.name: Supercharge latch
cards.summary: A supercharge floor tag raises a damage flag bit that latches supercharge until the tag is gone
cards.behavior: Standing on or touching a surface tagged supercharge sets bit 0x2000 in the accepted damage flags while preserving the low ten bits. Damage processing copies that bit into the supercharge latch each update and clears the latch as soon as the bit is missing, except in the immune state 44 where the latch is left alone. The latch is also cleared when the player body is reset on level entry.

cards.name: Portal level transition
cards.summary: A portal floor resolves a destination level and drives a path entity across the portal plane
cards.behavior: Touching a portal surface while health is not negative copies the first surface parameter as the destination level. Destinations above 64 are rejected and the current level is kept, which is how unfinished links were disabled. Otherwise the transition flag and portal index are stored, the current level is remembered as the return level unless it already sits at the start of its group, and the signed projection of the player-to-portal vector onto the portal normal picks the travel side: a negative projection reverses the half-length normal written as the path direction, a positive one uses it as is. A missing path link starts the plain transition state instead.

cards.name: Level entry and checkpoint placement
cards.summary: Entering a scene restores saved health, places the body, locks input briefly and arms flight levels
cards.behavior: Health is saved before a non-flight level load and written back after the scene is staged. When a checkpoint was stood on, the body is placed at the stored anchor and rotated to the stored angle; otherwise the scene header start position and rotation are used. The body is then reset and twelve gamepad updates are blocked. A level whose identifier ends in five becomes a flight level: the flying ability is set, the start height is remembered as the highest flight point and the flight state is forced. A checkpoint touch stores the anchor 356 units above the pad, the rotation scaled up and masked, the rescue and gem counters, and a copy of the killed entity bitset.

cards.name: Rescue scene entry and exit
cards.summary: Touching a rescue target starts a scripted scene that counts the reward and then hands control back
cards.behavior: The entry raises the per-level and total rescue counters, sets the heads-up counter, switches to the scripted gamestate with the screen border on, clears the scene state and tick counters, records the rescued entity and its scene index, releases the linked pad animation, plays the rescue sound and places the effect marker 64 units above the target. The exit restores the play gamestate with the border off, returns the linked pad to its idle state, resets the player without moving it, blocks gamepad updates for twelve frames, points the camera focus back at the player, clears the camera state and roll and installs a spherical preset before resuming.

constants.name: effectHeight
constants.unit: world units above the target, set once per rescue, rate unverified

constants.name: noLinkIndex
constants.unit: path link index, checked once per rescue, rate unverified

constants.name: inputLockUpdates
constants.unit: updates of blocked gamepad input, one per display frame, rate unverified

cards.name: Spherical follow camera
cards.summary: The camera orbits a focus point stored as azimuth, elevation and radius, with shoulder buttons supplying yaw
cards.behavior: A preset supplies azimuth, elevation and radius plus an offset triple that is copied into the live orbit. Azimuth is rebased against the focus rotation and masked to the 12-bit circle. The camera position is rebuilt from the radius: the horizontal pair is radius times cosine of elevation times cosine and minus sine of azimuth, and the vertical is radius times sine of elevation, all offset from the focus. View rotation takes elevation plus the offset elevation masked to the circle, and 0x800 minus azimuth minus the offset radius term, so orbit and roll stay coupled. Manual yaw resets its speed every update, writes -1024 while the right shoulder is held and 1024 for the left, and applies neither while centring is skipped or the player is off centre.

constants.unit: 12-bit angle units (wrap mask), applied per update, rate unverified

cards.name: Camera occlusion ray
cards.summary: A stepping ray between two camera points reports geometry in the way so the camera can pull in
cards.behavior: The vector between the two camera points is measured, its length divided by 1024 gives the number of segments, and the vector is shortened to a 1024-unit step. The step is walked from the first point, every segment is ray traced, and the first hit reports blocked so the caller can force the camera onto its destination; a full run with no hit reports clear. The check therefore has one step of granularity, and geometry thinner than one step between two samples is the only case that can slip through.

constants.name: rayStepShift
constants.unit: bit shift that turns ray length into segment count, applied per update, rate unverified

constants.name: raySegmentLength
constants.unit: world units per ray segment, stepped per update, rate unverified

cards.name: Stick calibration and input buffering
cards.summary: Sticks are recentred through a 48-unit deadzone and inputs are buffered across missed updates
cards.behavior: Calibration starts from a centre of 127 with min 0 and max 255, and re-centres whenever the stored centre is closer than 48 units to either end. Values outside the deadzone are rescaled back to the full range with sensitivities of 0x4000 above centre and 0x3f80 below and clamped to 0 or 255, while values inside the deadzone read as centred. On a stick controller the analog axes are also turned into digital directions at 193 and 64 when the direction pad is idle. Up to four missed updates are buffered, and when input arrives late the newly pressed and released buttons are merged into the pending ones instead of replacing them.
